artifacts.title: Smith v. Mississippi Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE William Smith complained against Mississippi Valley Presbytery's excommunication of TE Jeremy Smith who had confessed to adultery and abandoning his family. The SJC sustained one of the five allegations of error, finding that Presbytery incorrectly judged that the minister had 'refused' to appear since he was never formally cited, though the SJC did not annul the censure given other grounds for excommunication.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that McNeil's appeal was judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial, having refused to enter a plea or appear before Chesapeake Presbytery's Judicial Commission, and that his subsequent censure of suspension from the sacraments eliminated his standing to file further complaints against post-censure actions of the court.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.

artifacts.synopsis: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.

artifacts.title: Shive v. Central Carolina
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.

artifacts.title: Meaning of willful neglect and gross crime under BCO 46-5 and 30-4

matches.evidence: BCO 46-5 requires due process under BCO 27-5 for incorrigible members, and 'gross crime or heresy' is to be understood in its biblical and moral sense as determined by the church court.

artifacts.title: New case required to elevate indefinite suspension to excommunication

matches.evidence: The CCB found an overture requiring a new judicial case and process before indefinite suspension may be elevated to excommunication to be in conflict with the BCO.
